titleEn: Are schools a great equalizer? They help kids catch up, but wealthier children still pull ahead
titleZh: 学校能成为公平的起点吗？追赶的孩子与持续扩大的财富优势
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: In 1848, the education reformer Horace Mann called public schooling “the great equalizer of the conditions of men.” More than 175 years later, education scholars are still arguing about whether he was right.
paragraphs.zh: 1848年，教育改革家霍勒斯·曼（Horace Mann）称公立学校是“人类条件的伟大均衡器”。175年多过去了，教育学者们仍在争论他是否正确。

paragraphs.en: Some research finds that a child’s family background shapes their academic achievement far more than schools do. Other work finds that schools narrow academic achievement gaps that would otherwise be even wider.
paragraphs.zh: 一些研究发现，一个孩子的家庭背景对他们的学业成绩的影响远远大于学校。其他研究发现，学校缩小了学业成绩差距，否则差距会更大。

paragraphs.en: A classic study following Baltimore children in the 1980s found that low-income and wealthier kids learned at similar rates during the school year. Achievement gaps grew over the summer, when some children read with parents, visited libraries and went to camp, while others didn’t have those same opportunities. How much summer learning loss exists is still an open question.
paragraphs.zh: 20世纪80年代，一项对巴尔的摩儿童进行的经典研究发现，低收入家庭和富裕家庭的孩子在学年中的学习速度相似。成绩差距在夏季扩大，一些孩子与父母一起阅读，参观图书馆，参加夏令营，而其他孩子则没有同样的机会。夏季学习损失有多大仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。

paragraphs.en: But the larger point holds: Gaps between rich and poor children in reading and math skills are already large on the first day of kindergarten, driven by factors outside of K-12 schooling. For a given group of students, those gaps then stay about the same size through the school years.
paragraphs.zh: 但更重要的一点是：受K-12学校教育以外的因素影响，贫富儿童在阅读和数学技能上的差距在幼儿园的第一天就已经很大。对于特定的学生群体，这些差距在整个学年中都保持不变。

paragraphs.en: I am a scholar of education policy who studies the different factors that shape students’ learning, including teachers and the quality of their instruction.
paragraphs.zh: 我是一名教育政策学者，研究塑造学生学习的不同因素，包括教师和他们的教学质量。

paragraphs.en: Instead of measuring how much students learn at school, as is often the case, my colleagues and I recently measured what students receive in and out of school: the school funding, education support services and time that schools, government programs and families put into each child.
paragraphs.zh: 我和我的同事们没有像往常一样衡量学生在学校里学到了多少，而是衡量了学生在学校内外得到了什么：学校资金、教育支持服务以及学校、政府项目和家庭投入到每个孩子身上的时间。

paragraphs.en: By some measures, schools really are an equalizer for children from different backgrounds – but this finding has its limits.
paragraphs.zh: 从某种程度上说，学校确实是不同背景儿童的均衡器，但这一发现也有其局限性。

paragraphs.en: A gap that starts early in childhood
paragraphs.zh: 一个从童年早期就开始的差距

paragraphs.en: In our 2026 study, we combined data from 10 nationally representative government surveys to track 77 kinds of investments, as we call them, that contribute to raising and educating children. This includes teachers, tutoring, housing, food and childcare. We also measured factors that don’t have a direct cost, such as the time parents and caregivers spend reading with children.
paragraphs.zh: 在2026年的研究中，我们综合了10项具有全国代表性的政府调查的数据，追踪了77种我们称之为有助于抚养和教育儿童的投资。这包括教师、辅导、住房、食品和儿童保育。我们还测量了没有直接成本的因素，比如父母和看护人与孩子一起阅读的时间。

paragraphs.en: We put a dollar value on each factor – valuing parents’ time at the average U.S. hourly wage, for example – so we could add them up and compare what children from different backgrounds receive.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对每个因素都进行了美元价值评估-例如，以美国平均时薪来评估父母的时间-这样我们就可以将它们加起来并比较来自不同背景的孩子得到了什么。

paragraphs.en: Counting government investment, family spending and the time parents spend with their children, the average child in the U.S. receives about US$502,000 from birth to age 18, our analysis shows.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的分析显示，算上政府投资、家庭支出和父母陪伴孩子的时间，美国儿童从出生到18岁平均获得约50.2万美元。

paragraphs.en: The gaps in how much different children receive start early.
paragraphs.zh: 孩子们接受的不同程度的差距很早就开始了。

paragraphs.en: Before age 5, children from the poorest fourth of families receive about $44,000 less in total investments than children from the richest fourth – marking a gap of 24%.
paragraphs.zh: 在5岁之前，来自最贫穷的四分之一家庭的儿童获得的总投资比来自最富有的四分之一家庭的儿童少约44，000美元-差距为24%。

paragraphs.en: Most of that early difference comes from housing and childcare costs.
paragraphs.zh: 早期的差异主要来自住房和儿童保育费用。

paragraphs.en: However, a striking pattern emerges as children transition into elementary school. The gap in total investment between the richest and poorest children is cut in half, from 24% to 12%.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，随着孩子们进入小学，一个惊人的模式出现了：最富有和最贫穷的孩子之间总投资的差距减少了一半，从24%减少到12%。

paragraphs.en: For Black children, the benefit of starting school is even greater. Investment gaps between Black and white children shrink from 20% in early childhood years to 7% once kindergarten begins.
paragraphs.zh: 对于黑人儿童来说，开始上学的好处更大，黑人和白色儿童之间的投资差距从幼儿期的20%缩小到幼儿园开始后的7%。

paragraphs.en: This matters because research shows that more school spending improves students’ achievement and long-term outcomes, especially for those from low-income families.
paragraphs.zh: 这一点很重要，因为研究表明，更多的学校支出可以提高学生的成绩和长期成果，特别是对那些来自低收入家庭的学生。

paragraphs.en: So why don’t achievement gaps close during the school years?
paragraphs.zh: 那么，为什么成绩差距在上学期间没有缩小呢？

paragraphs.en: Catching up vs. getting ahead
paragraphs.zh: 追赶vs.领先

paragraphs.en: Part of the answer is what money buys.
paragraphs.zh: 部分原因在于钱能买到什么。

paragraphs.en: Our research shows that once children are in school, those from the lowest-income families receive 72% more in tutoring and 68% more in special education than those from the highest-income families, and Black children receive more than twice as much tutoring as white children.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究表明，一旦孩子上学，来自最低收入家庭的孩子比来自最高收入家庭的孩子多接受72%的辅导和68%的特殊教育，黑人孩子接受的辅导是白色孩子的两倍多。

paragraphs.en: These services are meant to help students catch up. A dollar spent catching up is not the same as a dollar spent getting ahead.
paragraphs.zh: 这些服务旨在帮助学生迎头赶上。花一美元迎头赶上与花一美元领先是不一样的。

paragraphs.en: Tutoring has long been one of schools’ main catch-up tools, and since the pandemic, schools have leaned on it more than ever. It’s a reasonable bet. Studies that randomly assign students to tutoring find some of the largest test-score gains of any school program.
paragraphs.zh: 长期以来，家教一直是学校的主要补习工具之一，自疫情爆发以来，学校比以往任何时候都更加依赖家教。这是一个合理的选择。随机分配学生参加家教的研究发现，在所有学校课程中，一些学生的考试成绩提高幅度最大。

paragraphs.en: Schools serving many low-income students have long been able to use federal Title I money for tutoring. Pandemic relief money made a bigger push possible. Congress sent schools nearly $190 billion, and the largest round was divided among districts the same way as Title I money, so high-poverty districts got more.
paragraphs.zh: 长期以来，为许多低收入家庭学生提供服务的学校一直能够使用联邦《教育法》第一条规定的资金进行辅导。大流行病救济资金使更大的推动成为可能。国会向学校拨款近1900亿美元，最大一轮拨款与《教育法》第一条规定的资金一样，在各区之间分配，因此高贫困地区得到的更多。

paragraphs.en: By 2022-23, more than a third of public schools offered “high-dosage” tutoring, meaning frequent sessions in small groups. Schools serving more low-income students and students of color were more likely to offer it.
paragraphs.zh: 到2022年至2023年，超过三分之一的公立学校提供“高剂量”辅导，这意味着频繁的小组辅导。为更多低收入家庭学生和有色人种学生服务的学校更有可能提供这种辅导。

paragraphs.en: But for many low-income, Black and Latino students, tutoring wasn’t new.
paragraphs.zh: 但对许多低收入、黑人和拉丁美洲学生来说，辅导并不新鲜。

paragraphs.en: In our data, collected from 2014 to 2021, about 17% of school-age children were being tutored, including 25% of Black children and 19% of Latino children, compared with 14% of white children. For Black, Latino and low-income children who received tutoring, over 75% got that support from public schools.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们收集的2014年至2021年的数据中，约有17%的学龄儿童接受了辅导，其中包括25%的黑人儿童和19%的拉丁裔儿童，而白色儿童的这一比例为14%。对于接受辅导的黑人，拉丁裔和低收入儿童，超过75%的人从公立学校获得了这种支持。

paragraphs.en: Early in the recovery, at least, the share of students getting tutoring didn’t appear to grow much. A nationally representative survey of parents in fall 2022 found about 15% of students were being tutored.
paragraphs.zh: 至少在经济复苏的早期，接受家教的学生比例似乎没有太大增长。2022年秋季对家长进行的一项具有全国代表性的调查发现，约15%的学生接受了家教。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, the pandemic widened achievement gaps. Students in high-poverty districts still trail those in wealthier districts by more than students in the same grades did before the pandemic. Schools leaned harder on catch-up help that low-income, Black and Latino students were already getting. Federal relief money did help high-poverty districts recover. But even with that help, gaps remain wider than before the pandemic.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，疫情扩大了学生成绩的差距。与疫情前同年级的学生相比，高贫困地区的学生仍然落后于富裕地区的学生。学校更加依赖低收入、黑人和拉丁裔学生已经得到的补习帮助。联邦救济金确实帮助了高贫困地区的恢复。但即使有了这些帮助，差距仍然比疫情前更大。

paragraphs.en: Who gets ahead
paragraphs.zh: 谁领先

paragraphs.en: Catch-up help is only half the picture. Wealthier children also get more of the resources that help them pull ahead, in school and out.
paragraphs.zh: 补习帮助只是其中的一半，富裕的孩子也能得到更多的资源，帮助他们在学校内外取得进步。

paragraphs.en: Some studies show, for example, that low-income students and students of color are more likely than richer, white students to have newer, less experienced teachers. Our study documents the same pattern.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，一些研究表明，与富裕的白色学生相比，低收入家庭的学生和有色人种学生更有可能拥有新的、经验不足的教师。

paragraphs.en: The differences are even starker outside of school.
paragraphs.zh: 这种差异在学校之外更为明显。

paragraphs.en: In our data, wealthier families invest far more in music lessons, sports and other activities that can help kids get ahead.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们的数据中，富裕家庭在音乐课程、体育运动和其他有助于孩子进步的活动上的投资要多得多。

paragraphs.en: Related research shows that by 2024, the richest 10% of families spent more than 13 times as much per child as the poorest quarter on childcare, education and extracurricular activities – up from about three times as much in the early 1980s.
paragraphs.zh: 相关研究显示，到2024年，最富有的10%家庭在儿童保育、教育和课外活动方面的人均支出是最贫穷的四分之一家庭的13倍以上，而上世纪80年代初的这一数字约为三倍。

paragraphs.en: Equal spending isn’t enough
paragraphs.zh: 平均支出是不够的

paragraphs.en: Our findings show that public education is the main reason the investment gap between rich and poor children shrinks once kids turn 5.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究结果表明，公共教育是富人和穷人孩子之间的投资差距缩小的主要原因，一旦孩子满5岁。

paragraphs.en: But equal spending is not equal opportunity. Much of the extra school spending on low-income, Black and Latino children goes to making up for gaps that opened before they started school. Meanwhile, wealthier children keep getting more of the experienced teachers and enrichment that help them pull ahead.
paragraphs.zh: 但平等的支出并不意味着平等的机会。低收入、黑人和拉丁裔儿童的额外教育支出，大部分都是为了弥补他们入学前的差距。与此同时，富裕家庭的孩子不断得到更多有经验的教师和丰富的教育，这有助于他们取得进步。

paragraphs.en: If schools are going to be a true equalizer – closing gaps, not just keeping them from growing – more catch-up help won’t be enough on its own. These students also need more of what helps their wealthier peers get ahead. And because the widest gaps open before kindergarten – in housing and childcare, where public support is thinnest – closing them can’t be left to schools alone.
paragraphs.zh: 如果学校要成为真正的均衡器--缩小差距，而不仅仅是阻止他们成长--那么仅靠更多的追赶帮助是不够的。这些学生还需要更多帮助他们富裕的同龄人取得成功的东西。而且，由于在幼儿园之前存在最大的差距--在住房和儿童保育方面，公共支持最薄弱--关闭它们不能仅靠学校。
